about: Partita for three (Torino 1787, «Del giuoco di Partita in tre persone», pp. 87-88): the game of four, played by three: «non altro hassi a fare, che mischiare, … regole sovradette; poi scartare, e giuocare». No calling, no exchange, no partner; whoever can count more points alone wins, «e si può guadagnare benissimo per una carta sola, e scompagnata». The book gives neither the number of cards nor the count nor the payment; the deal is taken from the three-player deal of p. 59 (25, 25, 28; the dealer puts three away), as Dummett (1980, p. 260) does; the payment is the agreed stake. Marks: [D] documented, [R] our reading, [S] sources silent.

dummett1980.cite: Michael Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London: Duckworth, 1980, chapter XIII «Tarocco in Piedmont and Lombardy», pp. 258-279 (our scan is partial: printed page 268 is missing)

torino1846.cite: L. B., Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, part I (Grammatica del giuocatore), Torino, Serra, [1846]

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 87: «Anche fra tre persone giuocar puossi in Partita».

direction.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 37: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo»: play passes to the right.

first_dealer.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 16 (general rule): cards are turned up and «se viene prima da questa parte un Trionfo, mischierò io»; the game sections themselves do not repeat who deals first, so the general rule is carried over.

cut_by.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 58 (Permesso, said before the deal): «ed a sinistra coppati»; who cuts is not named. Read with the general rule of pp. 16-18 as the player on the dealer's left; other reading: only the direction of the cut is meant.

cut_min.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 16: «Una carta sola non si può coppare»: a cut leaves at least two cards in each part.

dealer_rotation.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 70: after a hand that «si deve ripigliar da capo» «tocca al compagno appresso a mischiare, e dar i Tarocchi»: the next player deals; the book names no other change of dealer, and «appresso» is read in the direction of play (to the right).

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 88: «Chi dei tre compagni … contare più punti … nè cambiare alcuna carta».

signals.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 73: knocks and signs are barred «a qualunque altro giuoco di Tarocchi».

deck.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 88: dealt «secondo le regole sovradette», i.e. as the three-player deal of p. 59 (25 + 25 + 28 = 78); the number is not printed in the Partita pages.

trump_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 9-10, 13: the trionfi rank by their printed numbers, with the Angel XX above the World XXI («l'usanza, che in questo caso fa legge»); checked on the scan on 2 November 2026.

suit_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 11-13: swords and batons run 10 down to 1, cups and coins 1 up to 10, the courts above every numeral in the order King, Queen, Knight, Jack; checked on the scan on 2 November 2026.

card_points.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14: king 5, queen 4, knight 3, jack 2, Angel, Bagatto, Fool 5; plain cards counted with a figure in pairs (p. 52), our reading.

fool.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 90: «Il Folle si mostra», said for Partita of four; carried over to three.

fool_exchange.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 52, 90: «Il Folle si mostra» in the Partita pages; the card owed for the Fool (p. 52) is carried over from Venticinque, not printed in the Partita pages.

fool_exchange_card.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 52: «una cartaccia, qualunque gli piaccia».

fool_no_tricks.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 50: «non sarò io obbligato a dartelo mai»; Prammatica [1846], p. 6 disagrees («cederlo»), not followed.

replace.what: the Fool of a player who won no trick: kept or given up

options.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 87-88: no payment is printed; Dummett 1980, p. 260 («apparently» a fixed sum from each loser) is not a source of the book; the stake is agreed before the deal (p. 21); the choices are ours.

hand_size.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 88: «dare secondo le regole sovradette», the three-player deal of p. 59: 25 to each of the others. Dummett 1980, p. 260 reads it the same. Nice 1930, p. 284 deals three players the same (25 and 28).

replace.what: the deal, the discard and the payment of Partita for three

dealer_extra.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 88 and p. 59: the dealer takes 28; Dummett 1980, p. 260: three more cards for the dealer's discard. Nice 1930, p. 284 deals three players the same (25 and 28).

replace.what: the deal, the discard and the payment of Partita for three

packets.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 59: the way of dealing is the dealer's, announced before the cut («secondo le regole sovradette»).

packets_announced.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 59: announced before the cut.

order.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 59: «principiando sempre da tua destra».

who.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 88: «scartare» after the deal; only the dealer has cards over (p. 59).

count.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 88: the three over of p. 59.

count_mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 59, 88: exactly three, as at Permesso for three.

discard_honours_barred.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 90 «Il Folle si mostra, Bagatto non iscartasi, … secondo è stato detto di sopra» (said for Partita for four): the honours of rule 38 (p. 34) are not put away.

allowed_exceptions.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 34 (rule 38): «eccetto che Bagatto sia solo, senza il Folle»: «solo» is read as the only trump of the hand, as Dummett 1980, p. 259 reads this rule («neither the Folle nor any other trump»). Revision 1 read it as «holding no Fool». Page 90 says flatly «Bagatto non iscartasi» (of Partita for four). Other reading: no exception, as the rules of 1830 have it (Dummett, p. 259).

counts_for.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 87-88 do not say whose points the discard joins; ours: the discarder's, as in Venticinque (p. 55).

replace.what: the discard of a player who won no trick: kept or lost

announce.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 60: after «ho scartato» the discard cannot change.

first_leader.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 61: «Quando io abbia ritirato queste carte … e sia primo in mano, allor io giuoco»; the lone player leads, read as: because he, or whoever may lead, is the first in hand. Other reading: the lone player always leads. Elsewhere the general rule of p. 35 («Chi è a destra di chi dà, comincia») gives the lead to the player on the dealer's right, and Dummett 1980, p. 266 says the same for Permesso.

next_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 37: «Colui, che or ultimo ha preso la mano … deve essere il primo a giuocare».

follow_suit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 35: «debbon rispondere con carte della medesima sequenza».

must_trump.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36, for Partita and «anche negli altri giuochi»: «si risponderà e prenderà con un Trionfo». Torino 1787, p. 36 only shows it.

must_overtrump.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 36-37: a trionfo is answered with a trionfo and the higher takes; the book states no duty to beat the trump on the table (the fourth player «mette giù un Trionfo maggior» in the example, as a choice).

fool_may_lead.source: [S] Ours: the book does not say whether the Fool may be led; as in Venticinque (and p. 77 «solamente si mostra, quando cada in acconcio») it may be shown at any turn.

count_unit.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 88: a single unpaired card decides («per una carta sola, e scompagnata»); the half-point arithmetic of pp. 51-52 is carried over.

group.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 88-89: the Partita pages say «a quattro a quattro, o a due a due» only for four players; Dummett 1980, p. 260: «counted in twos; there are 91 points … odd low card counts ½ point».

odd_card.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 88: «per una carta sola, e scompagnata, che si abbia di più degli altrui punti»: an unpaired card counts.

fool_card.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 88 is silent on the Fool's card; ours: counted.

winner.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 88: «Chi dei tre compagni può contare più punti da se solo … questi guadagna».

tie.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 88 does not say what equal points are worth; ours: no one gains, the hand is replayed.

game_points.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 87-88 name no game points; the hand is settled in stakes.

unit.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 87-88: no payment is printed; the agreed stake.

mode.source: [R] Dummett 1980, p. 260 (not printed in the Turin book): the winner is paid by both the others; the book says only that he wins.

replace.what: the deal, the discard and the payment of Partita for three

amount.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 87-88: nothing is printed; the simple stake agreed before the deal (p. 21). Dummett 1980, p. 260 reads the same: the winner «is paid by both opponents; apparently the payment is fixed»; the game is not in the rules of 1830.

replace.what: the deal, the discard and the payment of Partita for three

kind.source: [S] Ours: the book describes one hand and prints no payment; the marche are settled after every deal, the match ends after one round of dealers (match.dealer_rounds); the greatest balance wins, equal balances are a draw («pace»).

dealer_rounds.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 87-88 are silent on the length of a match, and Torino [1846] has no Partita for three. Ours, by analogy with Venticinque for three, which is dealt the same way (25, 25, 28) and whose partita is made «in tre scarti» (Torino [1846], part I, p. 34): three deals, each player dealing once. The table may agree on two or three rounds.

replace.what: the length of a match in Partita for three, Dottore and Meno

effect.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 38 (general rule 35, said for Sedici; p. 79 (Meno) and p. 90 (Partita) send to it): «incorrere nella pena accennata … num. 35. di … tutti i giuocatori compagni»; the engine refuses a card that does not follow suit.

[D] Torino 1787, p. 73: «costui pagherà la partita semplice a tutti … giuocare, o far cessare il giuoco»; named for Permesso for three, four and five and for Chiamare il Re (and «a qualunque altro giuoco di Tarocchi»). [R] who the offender may be is not said (any player); the table cannot see a knock, so only the rules page tells it.
